reports.title: Consumer Price Index (CPI)
reports.description: The Gambia's national CPI. Directly verified via pdftotext extraction of the March 2024 release: "The Gambia Bureau of Statistics presents to users the Consumer Price Index (CPI) based on January 2019 =100 (Re-referenced to January 2020=100). The CPI is published on 15th of every month for the preceding month." Table headers in the same document use "COICOP" directly ("COICOP ALL ITEMS(JANUARY 2020=100)"), confirming the classification standard from GBoS's own primary document. GBoS's downloads listing confirms monthly releases through at least October 2025.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly, published on the 15th of the following month per GBoS's own release.

reports.title: Local Government Act, 2002 (No. 5 of 2002)
reports.description: UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF/G.23, confirmed s.130's referenced finance law is the Local Government Finance and Audit Act 2004, added verbatim s.130 text): The Gambia's Local Government Act. Directly verified via pdftotext extraction, Part VII (Financial Provisions), Section 128: "(1) The revenue and funds of a Council include all sums of money or funds accruing to a Council. (2) The revenue and funds of a Council shall be applied to the administration, development and welfare of the inhabitants within its Area of jurisdiction. (3) The Central Government shall provide twenty-five per cent of the Council's development budget." Section 131 separately grants Councils independent rating/taxation power (General Rates Act, 1992); Section 130 defers detailed financial regulation to a not-yet-located "Local Government (Finance and Audit)" law, stating in full: "The financial affairs of a Council shall be regulated in accordance with a Local Government (Finance and Audit) law to be enacted by the National Assembly." This referenced law was confirmed this round (AF/G.23) to be the "Local Government Finance and Audit Act, 2004" — cited by name and year in two independent primary Gambian government sources (the National Audit Office's audit report on Kanifing Municipal Council, see gm-nao-audit-kmc-2017-2019, and Kanifing Municipal Council's own budget page, see gm-kmc-budget-2021) — though its full text could not be located online at any government, NGO, or legal-database source despite exhaustive search (NAO's own "Laws & Standards" listing page omits it). No broader equalisation/formula-based revenue-sharing mechanism across the 5 divisions was found beyond this single 25% development-budget clause.

dependencies.basis: The specific attribution comes from the IMF's own ROSC (Report on the Observance of Standards and Codes) Data Quality Assessment Framework for The Gambia, describing GBoS's practice: "the general framework for compiling the CPI is the ILO CPI compilation manual and COICOP is used in the classification... The classification of COICOP follows Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose (COICOP) 1999 which is in conformity with international standards." This is IMF-authored (a third-party assessment of GBoS), not GBoS's own methodology note, but is the most specific documented evidence of the actual dependency — GBoS's own CPI release corroborates only the COICOP classification directly (table headers), not the manual name. `cpi-manual` already exists in the corpus (used by 8 other countries including Niger, Algeria, Morocco, Rwanda, Tunisia, Tanzania, Uganda, South Africa) — reused per the branch's node-id discipline.

An AU/StatAfric-authored Peer Review of The Gambia's National Statistical System (August 2025, EU-funded Pan-African Statistics Programme II) states: "the statistical work is guided by the African Charter on Statistics and the UN Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics and other international statistical [standards]" and "The main purpose of the Peer Review was to assess the GBoS's compliance with the African Charter." Third-party (AU/StatAfric), not GBoS-authored, and describes the National Statistical System broadly rather than the CPI specifically — 'cites' rather than 'methodology_depends_on' to reflect that weaker basis. `african-charter-statistics-2009` already exists in the corpus (first reused since the Tanzania precedent in af-grok-synthesis.json).
